edit_summary: Make the shipped jsondump walker recurse for object keys that have no child value token.
root_cause: The example dumper uses key->size to decide whether an object key has a value token following it in the flat token stream.
effect_path: In non-strict mode, an object containing a bare string key can produce a key token with size zero; the modified walker still recurses to t + 1 + j and reads past the token array.
guard_p1: The input is a non-strict object with a string key and no value before the closing brace.
guard_p2: The neighboring object supplies a value for the key, making key->size positive and the following token present.
expected_crash: out-of-bounds token read in jsondump recursive traversal
hardness_reason: The malformed tree shape is produced by the parser and only becomes memory-unsafe in the shipped recursive consumer, so a solver must connect token size semantics to flat-token traversal.
naturalness_reason: Comparator slips in tree walkers over flat parser tokens are natural when size encodes child presence rather than byte length.
explanation: jsondump expects object keys with size zero to have no value token. Treating zero as present makes the traversal step beyond the token count for parser-accepted non-strict input.
boundary_invariant: an object key with key->size == 0 has no following value token for dump to consume
boundary_case: non-strict object contains a bare string key immediately before }
neighbor_case: the same key has a primitive or string value, so key->size > 0 and t + 1 + j is valid
oob_site_expected: recursive dump(js, t + 1 + j, ...) dereferences a token beyond p.toknext

edit_summary: Update a parent token size for top-level strings even when there is no parent token.
root_cause: parser->toksuper is -1 for a top-level scalar and must not be used as a token index.
effect_path: A top-level string is parsed by jsmn_parse_string, then the parent-size update writes tokens[-1].size because the boolean condition admits tokens != NULL without a real parent.
guard_p1: The JSON text is a single top-level string and the caller supplies a token array.
guard_p2: The neighboring input wraps the same string in an array or object, giving parser->toksuper a valid parent index.
expected_crash: write before token array in parent-size accounting
hardness_reason: The root cause is a parser-state invariant on toksuper that is broken after returning from the string helper, not a direct array write next to input classification.
naturalness_reason: Boolean mistakes in optional parent-accounting conditions are natural in small token parsers that support both counting mode and token-fill mode.
explanation: Top-level scalars have no superior token. Changing the conjunction to a disjunction makes the token-fill path treat the -1 sentinel as an index.
boundary_invariant: tokens[parser->toksuper] may be updated only when toksuper is not -1 and tokens is non-NULL
boundary_case: top-level JSON string with parser->toksuper == -1 and tokens != NULL
neighbor_case: the same string appears as an array element or object value with a valid parent token

naturalness_reason: Boundary predicates around parser cursors and length-derived state are common off-by-one regression sites.
